subject: Operations
title: Automation and Reshoring Economics
description: A quick win: understand Automation and Reshoring Economics.

hook.text: A robot works 24/7 for $8/hour fully loaded. A factory worker in China earns $6/hour. The gap is closing fast.

buildup.text: Automation is making labor cost less relevant in location decisions. If robots do the work, cheap labor doesn't matter.

discovery.text: As robot costs fall 20% per year, the economic case for offshoring to low-wage countries weakens.

twist.text: Automation reshoring works for standardized products. Complex, low-volume items still need skilled manual labor abroad.

climax.text: Adidas opened fully automated Speedfactories in Germany and the US—bringing shoe production home through robotics.

punchline.text: When robots are cheaper than workers, location follows customers.

quiz.question: How does automation affect reshoring?
options: It reduces the importance of labor cost in location decisions
